$comment: Known-failing eval rows, as DATA — adding or removing one is a config edit, never a code change.
WHAT THIS IS NOT: this file does NOT affect `eval/run.mjs`, its verdicts, or its exit code.
`pnpm eval` stays red while a real defect is open, because it is also a release gate and a gate
that goes green over an open defect is worse than no gate. This file is read ONLY by
`scripts/eval-gate.mjs` (`pnpm gate`), and only to decide whether a failing row should BLOCK a
task from being called done. Acknowledgement is a property of the gate's report, not of grading.
WHAT AN ENTRY MEANS: 'this row is failing, we know why, it is filed, and a human decided it must
not block unrelated work until it changes'. It does NOT mean 'hidden'. Every acknowledged row is
still NAMED on every gate run, with its issue id — closing the report does not close the
obligation to chase the vendor or retire the capability (L-2).
STALE ENTRIES BLOCK, AND THAT IS THE POINT: when an acknowledged row starts passing, or stops
appearing in the matrix at all, the gate fails and names it. Without that, this list would only
ever grow — a blindfold assembled one honest decision at a time. Clearing a stale entry costs
one line of JSON, which is why blocking on it is the cheapest guard here.
KEY: '<chain>/<capability>', exactly as the eval reports them. A chain-less row (the server and
registry checks) uses the em-dash the eval itself prints: '—/<capability>'.
`issue` MUST reference a record that exists in docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md. An acknowledgement without
a filed issue is just silence with extra steps.

base/token.holders.why: Re-measured 2026-08-21 (task 014-42, scripts/probe-blockscout-holders-latency.ts). The 5s hop ceiling this entry was written against is gone: token.holders now runs at HOLDERS_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000 under a 60_000 deadline, and ethereum, arbitrum, polygon and gnosis all answer — their rows were cleared from this file by the same task. base did NOT recover: across three probe rounds it answered once, at 45.8s, and returned HTTP 500 or nothing otherwise, on the PRO facade and on the keyless base.blockscout.com alike. Same day, /api/v2/stats on base answered in 0.99s, so this is that chain's holders index and not the host. NOT a ceiling problem any more, which is why raising it further is not the next move: L-12's remaining half is one chain's index, and the open options there are the paid route or retiring the capability on base.
